technical: The comparison table says the default run had 0 process spans linked to the producer, but the default-run output in the post doesn't include that measurement. A reader can't check the cell that makes the two shapes look distinct. Fix: Add the 'default run, consumer spans linked to the producer: N' and 'default_receive_span links to the producer: N' lines from 05-fix.log to the proof block, so every table cell has a logged value next to it.

Every headline number traces to a corroborated contract measurement: 400 of 400 messages share a trace (05-fix.log:37), the header root matches the producer span (05-fix.log:50), Splunk shows 10 of 10 sampled traces, and receive spans rise from 0 to 76.

The comparison is controlled. The jar hash, the agent version (2.33.1) and the effective settings are checked on each pod. Only one setting changes between the default and receive telemetry runs, and receive spans act as the positive control.
The default-run table cell 'Linked to the producer: 0' has no line behind it in the output the post shows, although fix.sh prints that value.

The clone path in Step 1 (showmerit/labs/follow-sqs-messages-through-splunk-apm-with-the-otel-java) differs from this run's LAB_URL (Abhimanyu9988.github.io/labs/follow-sqs-messages-through-splunk-apm-w), so the post can't be reproduced as written.
The reader and their decision are clear: roll out the agent alone before asking teams for code. The opening delivers that answer with a count.

The trade-offs are honest. The post weighs one trace per message against a linked trace per consumer, covers the propagator alternative, and lists what wasn't tested (batch listeners, FIFO, SendMessageBatch, overhead).

The headline result, 400 of 400 in one trace, confirms what the maintainer already says in discussion 14193. The findings that go beyond the docs get less space: the link sits on the process span, not the receive span, and one receive span can hold two messages.

The output blocks look like a real session, with raw IDs, kind=5 and odd label names. In places the prose rhythm is even and reads as templated, for example 'Below: how the trace crosses the queue...'.

The only demand evidence is one GitHub discussion, opened in July 2025, with 5 comments and 15 replies and one new question in June 2026. The brief rates it weak, and no search-volume data exists, so the score is capped at 3.
The title credits Splunk APM and the OTel Java agent with the result and promises 'zero code', which the lab supports. That is the right framing for platform engineers on Spring Boot with SQS.
The headline doesn't use the words the people in that thread use, such as 'producer and consumer in the same trace'. That limits how many searchers it will match.

claims.text: The Java instrumentation uses the AWSTraceHeader system attribute by default, and producer and consumer should share a trace by default
The AWSTraceHeader attribute doesn't count towards message size
otel.instrumentation.aws-sdk.experimental-use-propagator-for-messaging defaults to false and moves context into message attributes with the configured propagator
The maintainer says the propagator setting changes how context travels, not whether spans share a trace, and suggests it for a stand-in that doesn't keep AWSTraceHeader
The maintainer discussion notes exceptions for batch receives
Receive telemetry is experimental and off by default at v2.33.1
An init container or the OpenTelemetry Operator are common ways to deliver the agent jar in production
The README's one hour is a safe budget for the run
The default behaviour applies to teams using SqsTemplate and single-message @SqsListener methods in general, beyond this one lab run

brief.reader: Platform engineer running Spring Boot services on EKS that talk over Amazon SQS
brief.decision: Whether to roll out the OTel Java agent alone for queue tracing, before asking any team for code changes or extra settings
brief.question: With only the Java agent attached, do my SQS producer and consumer land in one trace, and do I need a setting for that?
brief.takeaway: You can follow a message across SQS in Splunk APM from one environment variable, on the OpenTelemetry Java agent's defaults, and you know the one setting that gives each consumer a linked trace of its own.
brief.adds: Existing pages name the settings and describe the system attribute. This post counts real messages on a real queue, shows the header on a waiting message next to the producer span's trace ID, and measures what one setting changes.
brief.open_question: Of 400 messages sent through a real SQS queue with the Java agent on its defaults, what percent have producer and process spans sharing one trace ID, and with receive telemetry on, how many of 100 stay in that trace and how many link to it?
tradeoffs: One trace per message by default, or receive telemetry with each consumer in a linked trace of its own
The AWSTraceHeader system attribute by default, or the configured propagator in message attributes

existing_pages.title: Springboot sqs instrumentation
existing_pages.covers: A maintainer explains that context travels in the AWSTraceHeader system attribute by default, that producer and consumer should share a trace by default, and that receive telemetry gives separate traces joined by a span link. It gives no per-message count on real SQS.

existing_pages.title: Message metadata for Amazon SQS
existing_pages.covers: Message system attributes, and AWSTraceHeader as the supported one, holding an X-Ray trace header string. It doesn't cover the Java agent.

existing_pages.title: Settings for the AWS SDK instrumentation
existing_pages.covers: The agent's AWS SDK settings and their defaults, including the propagator setting for SNS and SQS, which defaults to false.

existing_pages.title: AWS SDK instrumentation metadata, v2.33.1
existing_pages.covers: The instrumentation's settings at v2.33.1, including receive telemetry, off by default, which starts a new consumer trace with a span link to the producer.

existing_pages.title: Spring Cloud AWS
existing_pages.covers: How to send with SqsTemplate and receive with SqsListener, with its own Observability Support section.
